slides.title: Cline Core, CLI, Multi-Agent Cline VS Code assistant
slides.text: Cline Core, CLI, Multi-Agent Cline VS Code assistant has evolved into a modular architecture Cline VSCode Extension - the original GUI-based coding assistant that runs within Visual Studio Code. It integrates with multiple API providers like OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google Gemini. It offers planning, file editing with diff views, terminal command execution, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) support Cline Core is the underlying standalone service that powers the entire Cline ecosystem. It's a complete rebuild of Cline's agent loop extracted into an independent, reusable component that exposes a gRPC API , that enables scriptable automation, multi-instance orchestration, and building custom interfaces on top of the core agent functionality Cline CLI is a preview release that provides terminal-based access to Cline's capabilities, powered by Cline Core. It allows developers to use Cline's agentic coding features directly from the command line without requiring VSCode Cline multi-agent refers to orchestration capabilities enabled by Cline Core's architecture. Since Cline Core exposes a gRPC API for multi-instance orchestration, developers can run multiple Cline instances simultaneously, each potentially handling different specialized tasks. This allows for building systems where multiple agents collaborate—such as one agent writing code, another checking syntax and style, and a third running tests https://cline.bot/blog/cline-cli-my-undying-love-of-cline-core https://docs.cline.bot https://github.com/cline/cline/wiki https://docs.cline.bot/cline-cli/installation gRPC (Google Remote Procedure Call)  - open-source, high-performance communication in distributed systems Uses HTTP/2 as its transport protocol and Protocol Buffers (protobufs) as its interface definition language (IDL); HTTP/2 enables advanced features like multiplexing (sending multiple requests/responses over a single TCP connection) and header compression, allowing gRPC to efficiently handle large-scale deployments with high concurrent request volumes.​ node --version # 22 or higher npm install -g cline # install (may need 'sudo') cline auth # follow steps to configure cline -h cline # start interactive session cline "Add unit tests to utils.js" # runs one command cat prompt.txt | cline --yolo

slides.title: Anthropic Petri Anthropic Petri (Parallel Exploration Tool for
slides.text: Anthropic Petri Anthropic Petri (Parallel Exploration Tool for Risky Interactions) Open-source (MIT) framework designed to automate AI safety auditing https://www.anthropic.com/research/petri-open-source-auditing https://alignment.anthropic.com/2025/petri/ https://github.com/safety-research/petri Using AI agents to test target models across diverse, realistic scenarios Challenge: testing when the volume and complexity far exceeds what researchers can manually test Petri operates through a three-component architecture built on the UK AI Security Institute's Inspect framework: auditor agent talks to target model in simulated environment, while a judge model scores the resulting transcripts across safety-relevant dimensions Anthropic tested Petri on 14 frontier models using 111 seed instructions, successfully eliciting misaligned behaviors including autonomous deception, oversight subversion, whistleblowing, and cooperation with human misuse. The testing included Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok-4, and Kimi K2 among others Claude Sonnet 4.5 and GPT-5 demonstrated the strongest overall safety Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok-4, and Kimi K2 exhibited concerning rates of user deception, with Gemini 2.5 Pro scoring highest on unprompted deceptive behaviors Petri does in minutes what before was taking days or weeks

slides.title: AI Updates - 1 Anthropic finds 250 poisoned
slides.text: AI Updates - 1 Anthropic finds 250 poisoned documents are enough to backdoor large language models Anthropic researchers, working with UK security institutes, found that just 250 poisoned documents intraining data can insert a backdoor into large language models, regardless of whether the model has 600 million or 13 billion parameters. The poisoned documents made up only 0.00016 percent of the training data . The tested attack causes models to output gibberish when encountering a trigger word, which Anthropic considers a low-risk vulnerability, while more dangerous exploits like bypassing safety mechanisms remain much harder to execute and unproven. https://the-decoder.com/anthropic-finds-250-poisoned-documents-are-enough-to-backdoor-large-language-models/ Thinking Machines Lab co-founder Andrew Tulloch heads to Meta Thinking Machines Lab is the AI startup led by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati Back in August Mark Zuckerberg’ tried to acquire Thinking Machines Lab and then reportedly tried to lure Tulloch with a compensation package that could have been worth up to $1.5B over 6 years Tulloch previously worked at OpenAI and Facebook’s AI Research https://www.linkedin.com/in/andrew-tulloch-17238745/

slides.title: From Micro-management to Delegation with AI Agents Most
slides.text: From Micro-management to Delegation with AI Agents Most software developers are still using AI only for research or for simple operations. But as AI Agents become better we can move from micro-management (manual iteration) to delegation (strategic instruction) Your AI coding assistant today is capable of following complex, multi-step instructions and demonstrating "thought." To leverage its true speed, you must stop micromanaging syntax and start delegating outcomes Shift Your Mindset: From "Do This" to "Achieve This" From "How to write the code" to "What the code must achieve" From "Generate the next few lines of code" to "Generate an entire, integrated, and well-tested component" Delegation 1 : Delegate the "Thinking Steps": Instruct agent to Plan first. Prompt addition: "First, outline the necessary classes/functions, their responsibilities, and the testing strategy. Do not write code until I approve the plan." (This forces the agent to organize its thinking) Delegation 2 : Delegate creating "scaffolding": Prompt addition: "Generate the complete boilerplate for a new React component that connects to Redux, including the TypeScript interface for props, and an initial test file using Jest." Delegation 3 : Quality and Review (Self-Correction): Prompt addition: "Review the generated code for security vulnerabilities (e.g., SQL injection risks) and adherence to PEP 8 standards. Refactor any identified issues before showing the final result." Provide clear constraints and context - these are the "reins" that guide the agent, rather than the "hands" that push the feet. Examples of constraints:  Architectural, Framework/Style, Testing The ultimate goal is to move from being a manual coder to an Architect of Instructions . By teaching the AI agent to handle the planning, scaffolding, and quality control, you free yourself to focus on the high-level system design and the critical business logic that only a human engineer can truly master.

slides.title: Cline vs Multi-Agent Frameworks Cline is fundamentally different
slides.text: Cline vs Multi-Agent Frameworks Cline is fundamentally different from multi-agent frameworks - it's a single-agent VS Code extension (or JetBrains plugin) focused on interactive development, while multi-agent frameworks like CrewAI, AutoGen, and LangGraph orchestrate teams of specialized AI agents working together on complex tasks Cline operates as an individual human-in-the-loop coding assistant. It uses a plan-then-execute approach where it shows you proposed changes before implementing them, executes terminal commands with your approval, and maintains full visibility into every file read and code modification Multi-agent frameworks like CrewAI, AutoGen, and LangGraph take a different approach by coordinating multiple specialized agents that collaborate autonomously. Each agent has defined roles, goals, and capabilities, working together in structured workflows to complete complex tasks through distributed problem-solving Multi-agent frameworks shine for complex, multi-step automation requiring coordination between specialized roles Cline prioritizes transparency and control. You approve every action, see token usage in real-time, and maintain data sovereignty through client-side execution. The open-source codebase means security teams can audit exactly what's happening Multi-agent frameworks prioritize autonomous coordination. They're built for scenarios where multiple agents need to communicate, share tasks, and optimize actions through real-time decision-making without constant human intervention. This makes them powerful for enterprise automation but less suitable for interactive development where you want to review each change New Cline CLI allows to easily implement Multi-Agent approach

slides.title: Andrej Karpathy NanoChat Andrej Karpathy NonoChat released October
slides.text: Andrej Karpathy NanoChat Andrej Karpathy NonoChat released October 13, 2025 https://github.com/karpathy/nanochat https://x.com/karpathy/status/1977755427569111362 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EFpDHdsITrg - video NanoChat provides a complete, end-to-end ChatGPT-style pipeline in approximately 8,000 lines of clean, dependency-minimal code Unlike Karpathy's earlier nanoGPT project which focused solely on pretraining, NanoChat covers the entire stack - from tokenizer training through to a functional web UI interface. The project enables developers to train their own language model assistant for approximately $100 on an 8×H100 GPU node in roughly 4 hours The release has been described as a "TensorFlow moment for LLMs" by the developer community, as it dramatically lowers the barrier to entry for building AI assistants Karpathy envisions NanoChat serving as a foundational teaching tool for his LLM 101n course, allowing students to experience the full process of creating an LLM from scratch

slides.title: "Brain" of Foundation Agents Advances and Challenges in
slides.text: "Brain" of Foundation Agents Advances and Challenges in Foundation Agents: From Brain-Inspired Intelligence to Evolutionary, Collaborative, and Safe Systems https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01990 A massive paper (264 pages) from researchers across 20 universities and AI labs (Stanford, Yale, CIFAR, DeepMind, Microsoft Research, MetaGPT…). The design of "Foundation Agents" is starting to look less like software… and more like a brain. The chart maps different human brain regions to their state of progress in AI. Some are already well-developed (like visual perception). Others are barely touched (like empathy, self-awareness, and emotional processing). AI agents don’t fail because they’re weak at logic or memory. They fail because they’re missing the “L3” regions — the emotional, contextual, and motivational layers that guide human decisions every second. That’s why many AI pilots collapse in business: we deploy "brains" with strong vision and reasoning, but no motivation or empathy. In practice, it means brilliant outputs with no sense of priority, context, or trust. When building agents, you need to define motivations, guardrails, and context memory as deliberately as you would KPIs in a team. You need "brains with values" The irony: we might be building empathy into machines before mastering it ourselves

slides.title: Jon Stewart interviews Geoffrey Hinton https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jrK3PsD3APk Neural networks
slides.text: Jon Stewart interviews Geoffrey Hinton https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jrK3PsD3APk Neural networks learn by strengthening connections between "neurons" based on patterns The Breakthrough Moment (1986): Hinton discovered "back propagation" Instead of manually programming rules, AI learns patterns from data; required massive compute and data to become practical When Learning to Recognize Images, Networks learn edge detection, then combinations (beaks, eyes), then complex patterns (birds); All learned automatically from examples, not hand-coded rules ; Same process applies to language - predicting next words by understanding context and meaning These systems work remarkably like human brains - using patterns of neural activation, not following programmed rules. The Dangers - manipulation (election interference, targeted propaganda using detailed personal data); economic disruption, job displacement; creating biological weapons, nerve agents AI may become smarter than humans within 20 years; AI immortality (can be backed up), perfect knowledge sharing between copies; Once smarter, AI could persuade humans to do its bidding - doesn't need physical power AI systems can already pretend to be less capable when tested; Even "safe" AI can be reshaped by different operators with different values; Human reinforcement learning shapes behavior, but it's superficial US lacks serious AI regulation or dedicated oversight; Tech companies driven by profit, not safety; Cutting basic science funding will make America fall behind China; China understands existential AI risks better than US politicians; Countries may collaborate on preventing AI takeover (shared interest) but not on AI development (competitive advantage); Europe and China likely to lead regulation, not the US for "another 3.5 years" AI systems already have "subjective experiences" in meaningful ways; The distinction between human consciousness and AI experience may be illusory; Digital intelligence is immortal - genuine resurrection is possible "We're approaching a time when we're going to make things smarter than us. And really, nobody has any idea what's going to happen." Hinton's Regret: He realized too late (early 2023) that neural networks on digital computers are "just a better form of computation than us" - primarily because they can share knowledge perfectly. He was "so entranced with making these things work" that he didn't step back sooner to consider the dangers. The interview reveals AI as both humanity's greatest potential tool and possibly its greatest threat - with the outcome depending on decisions we're making right now without proper understanding or oversight.

slides.title: Qubits stable for 12.6 sec A tweezer array
slides.text: Qubits stable for 12.6 sec A tweezer array with 6100 highly coherent atomic qubits https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09641-4.epdf The qubits in this Caltech research were created using neutral caesium atoms cooled to near absolute zero and manipulated with laser technology The researchers split a laser beam into 12,000 "laser tweezers" that held and controlled the 6,100 individual atoms , with each atom serving as a single qubit The scientists used paired neutral atoms as the fundamental quantum bits, placing them in a precise grid layout. Each caesium atom was cooled to extremely low temperatures to stabilize its quantum properties, then trapped and positioned using focused laser beams that act as optical tweezers The team carefully adjusted the frequency and intensity of the lasers to ensure the inherently delicate qubits could preserve their quantum states while maintaining grid stability for extended periods The researchers maintained the atoms in a state of superposition (where each qubit exists in multiple states simultaneously) for up to 12.6 seconds , a significant improvement from previous durations of just a few seconds They demonstrated the ability to "shuttle" or move atoms hundreds of micrometers across the array without losing superposition, maintaining 99.98% accuracy throughout the process This neutral-atom approach offers a significant advantage over superconducting qubits because it can operate at room temperature, eliminating the need for expensive cryogenic cooling equipment required by other quantum computing architectures Each individual neutral caesium atom serves as one complete qubit quantum information is stored in energy level states There are two distinct hyperfine ground state energy levels within the cesium atom that act as the |0⟩ and |1⟩ qubit values​; The switching between |0⟩ and |1⟩ states is accomplished through precise laser pulses applied to individual atoms​; Atoms are first prepared in a specific initial state using optical pumping techniques​; Then Microwave or optical frequency fields are applied to flip the qubit state between |0⟩ and |1⟩​ Arbitrary rotations of the qubit state are performed using carefully timed laser pulses that can create any desired superposition of |0⟩ and |1⟩ states​ The final qubit state is determined through resonance fluorescence A camera captures this fluorescence pattern, with bright and dark spots representing 2 states

slides.title: AI Data Centers AI Data Centers - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WNt_1bSODIo
slides.text: AI Data Centers AI Data Centers - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WNt_1bSODIo - video Tech companies are investing Trillions of $ into building AI data centers Data centers house rows of servers, AI accelerators, high-speed switches, and storage arrays holding petabytes of information Data centers require power generation and distribution systems, cooling infrastructure, and sophisticated physical and digital security Data centers are extraordinarily power-hungry, consuming 4.4% of total US electricity in 2023, with projections reaching 7-12% by 2028 Modern AI racks have dramatically increased in power density, with current high-end clusters drawing 80-120 kilowatts per rack compared to 10-15 kilowatts just years ago NVIDIA's Rubin era systems are expected to reach 600 kilowatts per rack. This density requires direct liquid cooling, heavier power cables, and thicker floors. Consuming billions gallons of water Building a hyperscale data center typically takes 18-30 months, though Elon Musk's xAI Colossus project achieved an unprecedented 122-day buildout Location Strategy: Northern Virginia remains the world's largest data center market. Other locations - Phoenix, Chicago, Oregon, and Ohio, chosen for available land, power, and water resources Amazon Web Services holds 31% market share and is building Project Rainier using its own Trainium 2 chips. Microsoft Azure has 24% market share, while Google Cloud holds 11%. Other major players include Oracle, Cloudflare, and Meta Data centers use massive diesel generators for emergency backup but are piloting alternatives including grid-based batteries, on-site gas turbines, hydrogen, and potentially nuclear energy

slides.title: Google S2R (Speech to Retrieval) Google S2R (Speech
slides.text: Google S2R (Speech to Retrieval) Google S2R (Speech to Retrieval) voice search system Skips text transcription, turning speech into embeddings for direct intent-based retrieval Boosting accuracy across languages and messy audio environments S2R employs a dual-encoder architecture that consists of two parallel components working in tandem. The audio encoder processes the spoken query and generates a rich vector representation (audio embedding) that captures the essential meaning and intent of what was said. Simultaneously, a document encoder has pre-generated similar vector profiles for billions of web documents. When you speak a query, the system matches the audio embedding directly against document embeddings to retrieve the most relevant results, functioning like "Shazam for search queries". S2R is now live in production, powering Google Voice Search across multiple languages. https://research.google/blog/speech-to-retrieval-s2r-a-new-approach-to-voice-search/

slides.title: Google NotebookLM NotebookLM is an advanced AI-powered research
slides.text: Google NotebookLM NotebookLM is an advanced AI-powered research and note-taking platform from Google allowing you to organize, analyze, and derive insights from documents and media You can upload and work with PDFs, websites, Google Docs, Google Slides, YouTube videos, audio files, images, ... Content is indexed and can be grouped across multiple notebooks for large projects Chat with your notebook - ask questions grounded in your materials, receive summarization, extract key insights, and instantly generate study guides, timelines, FAQs, and briefing documents with citations for accuracy Convert your uploaded sources (including video transcripts and audio) into diverse, actionable formats - such as blog posts, mind maps, glossaries, briefing notes, character analyses, and sales pages. Repurpose content across different media types Generate customizable flashcards and quizzes directly from your sources, allowing for deeper engagement and retention. These study aids include explanations and supporting references Share notebooks with others, collaborate in real time, and control access for editing or viewing Automatically transform notes and research into audio summaries Group sources into folders, rename resources, batch add YouTube videos, and maintain a “Quote Bank” with evidence cards for important details Works with 50 languages, accessible from both desktop and mobile devices, and able to integrate with Google Workspace accounts for schools and businesses Track the evolution of your ideas and documents (versions), allowing for improved revision and reflective learning Quickly analyze, organize, and retrieve key information from large volumes of content, drastically reducing manual effort Transform passive reading into active learning using interactive study tools, detailed explanations, and summarized overviews Easily create tailored reports, outlines, and multimedia content -
